realism_constraints: No modern forensic DNA or electronic surveillance
Medical knowledge includes morphine poisoning and early sleeping sickness
Travel by horse-drawn carriage and early electric trains
location: London, specifically Kennington Lane and New Inn

cast.name: Dr. Jervis
cast.private_secret: investigating suspicious poisoning and will case

cast.name: John Thorndyke
cast.role_archetype: legal and medical jurist, master detective

cast.name: Mr. H. Weiss
cast.private_secret: disguised identity as John Blackmore, administering poison

cast.name: John Blackmore
cast.role_archetype: actor, stockbroker, suspected forger and murderer
cast.private_secret: forged will, impersonated brother, imprisoned Jeffrey

surface_summary: A mysterious patient suffering from morphine poisoning is secretly confined in a house in Kennington Lane. A forged will benefits John Blackmore, who impersonates his brother Jeffrey Blackmore, the victim. The investigation uncovers a conspiracy involving chronic poisoning, imprisonment, and identity fraud.
accepted_facts: Jeffrey Blackmore died and left a will favoring Stephen Blackmore
A second will was found, favoring John Blackmore, but was legally valid
Jeffrey Blackmore was addicted to opium and had poor eyesight
Mr. Weiss was a tenant in Kennington Lane with a housekeeper Mrs. Schallibaum
inferred_conclusions: The second will was genuine and reflected Jeffrey's true intentions
Mr. Weiss was an innocent tenant unrelated to the will dispute
Jeffrey Blackmore died by suicide as indicated by the porter
mechanism_description: John Blackmore impersonated his brother Jeffrey Blackmore, who was secretly confined and chronically poisoned in a house in Kennington Lane to enable John to inherit Jeffrey's estate by forging a second will. The man known as Mr. Graves was actually Jeffrey Blackmore, and the murder was orchestrated by John Blackmore and his accomplice Mrs. Schallibaum; their capture was secured by Thorndyke's investigation.
delivery_path: John Blackmore impersonates Jeffrey Blackmore at New Inn
Jeffrey Blackmore is secretly confined and chronically poisoned in Kennington Lane
A forged second will is executed by John Blackmore posing as Jeffrey
Dr. Jervis is called to treat the morphine-poisoned patient Mr. Graves
Thorndyke analyzes compass bearings to locate the secret house
Investigation reveals disguises, imprisonment fastenings, and unique spectacles
Police arrest John Blackmore and Mrs. Schallibaum after evidence is gathered
outcome_result: John Blackmore and Mrs. Schallibaum are arrested and charged with the murder and forgery, while Jeffrey Blackmore is identified as the secret prisoner.

false_assumption.statement: The second will was genuine and executed by Jeffrey Blackmore himself.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The will was signed in the presence of two unimpeachable witnesses who swore to the signatures and contents, and the body found was identified as Jeffrey Blackmore's. This gave the appearance of authenticity and legality.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: It conceals the fact that John Blackmore impersonated Jeffrey and forged the will, while the real Jeffrey was secretly confined and poisoned elsewhere.

supporting_points: He was the tenant of the suspicious house in Kennington Lane
He administered morphine poisoning to Mr. Graves
He used a closed carriage and elaborate secrecy
He had a motive related to the patient's condition
false_solution.the_one_flaw: He was actually John Blackmore in disguise, and the real Weiss was not involved.

red_herrings.description: Mrs. Schallibaum's changing appearance and squint suggested she was a different person.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: Her squint could be controlled and her appearance altered by makeup and disguise.

red_herrings.description: The suggestion that the patient suffered from sleeping sickness rather than morphine poisoning.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: The symptoms matched morphine poisoning and were confirmed by antidotes; sleeping sickness was unlikely.

closed_circle.rationale: Only these three had access to the patient and means to administer poison, and were connected to the suspicious house and forged will.

time_windows: September to March (period of signature change and poisoning)
Evenings and nights (patient's stupor and poisoning)

inference_path.observation: The patient Mr. Graves showed symptoms of morphine poisoning with no needle marks.
inference_path.correction: Morphine was administered orally or by other means, not self-administered.
inference_path.effect: Indicates poisoning by a third party.
required_evidence: Physical examination notes of Mr. Graves
Absence of hypodermic needle marks on patient's arms and legs

inference_path.observation: Compass bearings and timing from carriage rides to secret house.
inference_path.correction: Plotting bearings on map locates the house in Kennington Lane.
inference_path.effect: Identifies the secret location of the patient.
required_evidence: Notebook with compass bearings and timestamps

inference_path.observation: Spectacles found in Kennington Lane house match those prescribed to Jeffrey Blackmore.
inference_path.correction: Confirms patient Mr. Graves is Jeffrey Blackmore.
inference_path.effect: Identifies the secret prisoner as Jeffrey Blackmore.
required_evidence: Fragments of spectacles from Kennington Lane
Optician's and oculist's letters describing Jeffrey Blackmore's glasses

inference_path.observation: Second will executed in presence of witnesses and signed by 'Jeffrey Blackmore'.
inference_path.correction: John Blackmore impersonated Jeffrey to execute forged will.
required_evidence: Photograph of the cuneiform inscription hung upside down
Cabman's testimony of a woman accompanying a man to New Inn
Disguise and makeup materials found in Kennington Lane house

inference_path.observation: John Blackmore was known to be an actor and stockbroker with motive.
inference_path.correction: He had skills and opportunity to impersonate his brother and forge documents.
inference_path.effect: Identifies John Blackmore as the principal culprit.
required_evidence: Statements about John Blackmore's profession and character

inference_path.observation: Mrs. Schallibaum's presence and behavior in Kennington Lane house.
inference_path.correction: She was accomplice in imprisonment and poisoning.
inference_path.effect: Identifies her as an accessory to the crime.
required_evidence: Cabman's description of a woman with veil and bead fringe
Observation of Mrs. Schallibaum's squint and disguise

inference_path.observation: Poisoned sugar found in tea intended for Dr. Jervis.
inference_path.effect: Shows desperation and danger from culprits.
required_evidence: Sample of sugar tested positive for aconitine
Incident at tea-shop with Mrs. Schallibaum

discriminating_test.design: Thorndyke uses compass bearings and timing to plot the carriage route to the secret house, then visits the location to verify the presence of the house and its features, including the covered way and new macadam patch. He locks the gate to detect any unauthorized entry, confirming the presence or absence of suspects.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: This test confirms the exact location of the secret house and the presence of only authorized persons with keys, narrowing down suspects and confirming the concealment of Jeffrey Blackmore.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: The house is located at the plotted position with locked gates and no unknown persons entering during the observation period.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is given all necessary clues including the compass bearings, the peculiar spectacles, the inverted cuneiform inscription, the cabmen's testimonies, and the suspicious behavior of Mr. Weiss and Mrs. Schallibaum. The method of plotting the secret house's location is explained in detail, allowing the reader to deduce the concealment and impersonation. The subtle hints about the disguise and the identity of the victim and impostor are all present before the final explanation.
